idea: An AI note-taker for therapists that transcribes and summarizes therapy sessions.

final_schema.proposed_solution: An AI note-taker for licensed therapists.

_regression_note: The thin/one-sided evidence fixture (gap-closing plan Stage 6) -- deliberately NO 'supports' items at all. Exercises: (a) stance-slot reservation degrading correctly when one side genuinely has zero evidence, rather than padding with irrelevant material to force balance, and (b) the verdict's 'no confident filler' guardrail -- a verdict built only from this fixture should read low/medium confidence and an honestly weak case_for, not a fabricated strong one.

evidence_items.quote: AI transcription tools for therapy sessions face substantial HIPAA compliance burden, including business associate agreements and strict audio-retention rules that many small vendors underestimate.
Incumbent EHR vendors used by most therapy practices have already begun bundling AI note-taking features into their existing platforms at no extra cost.
There are an estimated 320,000 licensed therapists practicing in the United States as of the most recent labor statistics.
Several states require two-party consent before any session audio can be recorded, adding a compliance step before a note-taking tool can even be used.
